info.name: HMS — CORS & CSRF Demo
info.description:
Real Postman evidence for HMS v4, User Stories 1.2 and 3.2 (docs/v4/README-V4.MD) — replaces the earlier curl-only verification recorded in docs/v4/v4-report.md.

What this collection actually proves, and what it doesn't:
- The CORS folder inspects the RAW server response to an OPTIONS preflight for an allowed vs. a disallowed Origin. Postman itself does NOT enforce CORS the way a browser does (it's a native client, not a page subject to the same-origin policy) — this verifies the SERVER's own CorsConfigurationSource decision, not client-side enforcement. For the enforcement side (a real browser actually blocking the response), see the companion docs/v4/cors-browser-test.html.
- The CSRF folder relies on Postman's own per-domain cookie jar behaving like a browser's: the first GET stores the session cookie, and every later request in this collection to the same {{baseUrl}} automatically carries it — run the three CSRF requests in order (top to bottom, or via Collection Runner) for the token variable and cookie to be in place.

Set {{baseUrl}} (collection variable below) to your running instance — defaults to http://localhost:8080.

request.description: http://localhost:3000 is one of app.cors-allowed-origins (see application.yaml / .env). Expect the server to echo it back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

exec: pm.test("Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes the allowed origin", function () {

item.name: Preflight — disallowed origin (expect 403, no ACAO header)

request.description: http://evil.example is NOT in app.cors-allowed-origins. A real browser making this same request from that origin would block reading the response even if the server returned 200 — Spring's CorsFilter goes further and rejects the preflight outright.

item.name: 1. GET the demo page (stores session cookie + real CSRF token)

request.description: Postman's own cookie jar stores the session cookie Spring Security's CsrfFilter sets here, the same way a browser would — every later request to {{baseUrl}} in this collection carries it automatically.

exec: pm.test("CSRF token found in the rendered page", function () {

item.name: 2. POST with the real token (expect 200 — legitimate submission)

request.description: Run request 1 first so {{csrfToken}} and the session cookie are populated.

exec: pm.test("Response echoes the submitted note", function () {

item.name: 3. POST with no token (expect 403 — forged-request simulation)

request.description: Same session cookie as request 2 (Postman's cookie jar), but no _csrf field at all — stands in for a forged cross-site submission that has no way to know the token. CsrfFilter should reject this before CsrfDemoController.submit ever runs.
